record.paper_title: The Higgs program and open questions in particle physics and cosmology
record.original_question: Is the observed Higgs boson h—the scalar discovered by ATLAS and CMS whose measured properties are currently consistent with the Standard Model Higgs boson—the only scalar degree of freedom in the electroweak sector? More concretely, does h originate purely from an SU(2) gauge doublet, and if more than one Higgs doublet or other scalar field exists, is h exactly aligned with the vacuum-expectation-value direction v rather than mixed with additional scalar degrees of freedom?

evidence.quote:
Here is a list of seven open questions at the forefront of particle physics and cosmology, to which the Higgs program may provide answers:
1. Is h the only scalar degree of freedom?

The scalar h discovered in the ATLAS and CMS experiments [ 1, 2] has measured properties that are all consistent,
within present experimental accuracy, with the SM predictions for the Higgs boson [ 28]. The question that is being
asked is whether the observed Higgs boson is the SM Higgs boson. In fact, one can separate this question to two:
1. Does h originate from purely a doublet?
2. If there is more than a single doublet, is h in exactly the direction of v?

artifact.category_tag: Higgs sector and electroweak symmetry breaking
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the electroweak sector of a quantum field theory with gauge group SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y, in which electroweak symmetry is spontaneously broken to U(1)_em by the vacuum expectation value v ≈ 246 GeV of one or more complex scalar fields. Suppose a neutral CP-even scalar boson h of mass approximately 125 GeV has been observed, and that all of its currently measured couplings (to gauge bosons W, Z, to fermions, and its self-coupling where accessible) are consistent, within present experimental precision, with those predicted for the single Standard Model Higgs boson arising from a single SU(2)_L doublet Φ acquiring the vacuum expectation value v.

Address the following two questions:

(a) Is h the only fundamental scalar degree of freedom participating in electroweak symmetry breaking, i.e., does the scalar potential of the underlying theory contain only one SU(2)_L doublet whose neutral CP-even excitation is h, with no additional Higgs doublets, singlets, triplets, or other scalar multiplets contributing to electroweak symmetry breaking or mixing with h?

(b) If the scalar sector contains more than one SU(2)_L doublet (or further scalar multiplets) Φ_i with vacuum expectation values v_i satisfying Σ |v_i|^2 = v^2, is the physical mass eigenstate h exactly aligned with the direction of the total vacuum expectation value v in scalar field space — that is, is h the linear combination Σ (v_i / v) Re(Φ_i^0) with no admixture of orthogonal CP-even neutral scalar directions (the so-called exact alignment limit)?

Determine, on the basis of present and foreseeable experimental constraints together with theoretical consistency, whether (a) and (b) hold.
artifact.status_search_result: As of 2026, the LHC has measured Higgs couplings consistent with the Standard Model at the ~10% level, but extended scalar sectors (two-Higgs-doublet models, singlet extensions, MSSM Higgs sectors, etc.) remain viable and only constrained, not excluded. The exact alignment limit is favored but not established; small deviations remain experimentally allowed. The question of whether h is the unique scalar degree of freedom and whether it is exactly aligned with v is therefore open and is an active target of HL-LHC and future-collider Higgs precision programs.

status_evidence.title: Higgs boson coupling measurements at the LHC
status_evidence.snippet: Combined ATLAS+CMS measurements show Higgs couplings consistent with SM predictions within ~10% uncertainty, leaving room for BSM scalar sectors.
status_evidence.claim: Current Higgs coupling measurements are SM-consistent but allow extended scalar sectors.

status_evidence.title: Searches for additional Higgs bosons and constraints on 2HDM
status_evidence.snippet: Searches for additional neutral and charged Higgs bosons constrain but do not exclude two-Higgs-doublet models; the alignment limit is preferred.
status_evidence.claim: Extended Higgs sectors and deviations from exact alignment remain experimentally allowed.
